qwen3-8b.note: dense with per-head q/k RMSNorm (QK-norm), no GDN; native window 40,960 (max_position_embeddings, no RoPE scaling): runs at <= 32K only, no YaRN (decided 2026-10-04), so the 64K RULER cell and the long-prompt documents over 32K are not run; niah_format raw (its chat template thinks by default)

engine_tail: engine runs: tail start = (N - max(T, 512)) // block * block (his planner); the block size is read at server boot, the real tail is recorded per request, and the reference side of any comparison uses the same rounding (arm option tail_round, base >= 512). tail_round is refused with a select (rows would be picked against the unrounded boundary) and with tail_from

engine_tier.rule: v1.1.1 clarification of 'no non-deterministic runs' (not an exemption): engine-tier results are reported only with their tier label and the same-boot exact-vs-exact noise floor; an engine FINAL- run requires the deterministic top-k fix; pre-fix engine numbers appear only in the negative-results and lever tables, under prefix_label, never in a claim
engine_tier.final_requires: deterministic top-k (QSA indexer selection) in the engine build
engine_tier.prefix_label: engine, pre-deterministic-fix, run noise about +-0.01 nats/doc

c5_image.scope: v1.1.4: the C5 Flash-Next final tier only (FINAL-FLASHNEXT-C5); RidgeFill is built into this build (vllm/v1/ced.py, vllm/models/qwen4_exp/amd/ced.py). engine_image stays the image of all earlier engine work (27B, the 2026-10-04 Flash-Next development runs). v1.1.6: the C5 engine build is this image plus the overlay below, which meets final_requires; C5 results from the image alone (2026-10-08 to 2026-10-10) are pre-fix and carry prefix_label

overlay.mount: each file read-only over /opt/vllm/lib/python3.14/site-packages/vllm/<path>; the C5 kit checks the sums before boot and inside the running container (C5_ENGINE_OVERLAY)
overlay.fix: the deterministic top-k fix for 29.08.10: libr4d's fused QSA block select returns its blocks in a run-dependent order and breaks exact score ties run-dependently once it scores more than 2048 block columns (context above 8192 tokens; decode always); the overlay sorts the fused select's output ascending and, above 2048 columns, takes the block top-k in torch with exact ties to the lower block index, expanded by the engine's own Triton kernel, plus a NaN guard
overlay.verified: 2026-10-10, ridgefill-determinism-20261010 ledger D1-D9c: identical requests bitwise equal 3x on one boot and across two boots, exact and graded paths, prompt logprobs 8K-32K and greedy generation 16K-64K, and A-B-A on one boot; cost vs the image alone: prefill +0.0 to +1.5% (16K-64K), decode -5 to -7%

arms.noproj: fill identity: late layers' K/V and GDN updates from the layer-S state (POP-style; not POP itself). Paper: identity (POP's fill at our split and tail)
arms.kva: fill proj with the standard full-rank sweep projector of this split. Paper: ridgefill
arms.skip: fill none: prefix rows never reach the late layers (plain layer skip). Paper: nofill (the exact tail alone; POP's 'w/o Indep. KV' ablation, checks/T0.1)
arms.noproj+qattn5: noproj + exact rows: top 5% by question-window attention (legacy rows; the paper's rows arms are qattn10)
arms.kva+qattn5: kva + exact rows: top 5% by question-window attention (legacy rows; the paper's rows arms are qattn10)
arms.noproj+qblind5: noproj + exact rows chosen from the 64 rows before P only (question-blind)
arms.kva+qblind5: kva + exact rows chosen from the 64 rows before P only (question-blind)
arms.swiftkv: SwiftKV maps + exact tail: the SwiftKV checkpoint's trained maps fill the prefix rows' late K/V at its split; the exact tail and decode run the base model (Llama baseline; compare only at matched compute). SwiftKV as released is its own kind, swiftkv-native
arms.noproj+qattn10: noproj + exact rows: top 10% by question-window attention. Paper: identity+rows
arms.kva+qattn10: kva + exact rows: top 10% by question-window attention. Paper: ridgefill+rows
arms.noproj+qblind10: noproj + exact rows: top 10% chosen from the 64 rows before P only (question-blind: the selector reads the document only), at the blind split (T1.4)
arms.kva+qblind10: kva + exact rows: top 10% chosen from the 64 rows before P only (question-blind: the selector reads the document only), at the blind split (T1.4)
arms.pop-native: POP as published (arXiv:2602.03295; checks/T0.1): fill identity at the model's pop_split = L - floor(L/3), the exact tail = the scored rows, set per prompt ("tail_from": "continuation", no "tail"): grade 513, longppl the continuation + 1, generation sets 1 (POP's last prompt token run as the first decode step). Hybrids: GDN layers filled as ours (labelled)
arms.swiftkv-native: SwiftKV as released (fill swiftkv_native, no exact tail): every row's late K/V from SwiftKV's maps, queries through q_proj_swiftkv, prefill and decode; the baseline model at its split (R6; scripts/swiftkv_report.py pairs it with both exacts)
arms.kva+kexact: splice (T2.1, interventional; diagnostic: reads the true late inputs): kva with the late attention layers' prefix K from their true inputs (exact_part k), V filled
arms.kva+vexact: splice (T2.1): kva with the late attention layers' prefix V from their true inputs (exact_part v), K filled
arms.kvexact: splice (T2.1): K and V of every late attention layer from the true inputs; dense models: fill oracle (= exact prefill, a sanity row); hybrids: fill_by_type attention oracle, gdn proj with the sweep projector (the GDN-only error of kva)
arms.kva+ktail: kva with the filled prefix K of the late attention layers rescaled per KV head by the tail-measured norm ratio (rescale ktail; T2.2: a test on dense models, a demonstration on QK-normed ones)
arms.kva+vtail: kva with the filled prefix V rescaled by the tail-measured norm ratio (rescale vtail; appendix)
arms.noproj+random: random-rows control (T1.5): noproj + uniformly random exact prefix rows, as many as the rows arm named in select.match (same fill, split and tail, same config) picked on the same prompt
arms.kva+random: random-rows control (T1.5): kva + uniformly random exact prefix rows, as many as the rows arm named in select.match (same fill, split and tail, same config) picked on the same prompt
arms.noproj+tailmatch: tail-budget control for rows (T1.5): noproj, no exact rows; the exact tail grows by the row count of the rows arm named in select.match (same fill, split and tail, same config)
arms.kva+tailmatch: tail-budget control for rows (T1.5): kva, no exact rows; the exact tail grows by the row count of the rows arm named in select.match (same fill, split and tail, same config)
arms.skip+tailbudget: tail-budget control for the fill (T1.5): nofill with round(b x N) more exact tail rows (select start_recent, start 0, budget b; b declared in the FINAL record from the fill's measured or modelled cost)

depths_note: splits at 1/4, 3/8, 1/2 and 5/8 of the layers on the reference models (the engine models keep 1/4, 3/8, 1/2), on the boundary below for a non-integer depth (Qwen3-8B: 3/8 x 36 = 13.5 -> 13, 5/8 -> 22) and on a block boundary for hybrids (Flash-Next: 16 = 1/3, the boundary below 3/8, kept for continuity); pop-native runs at each model's pop_split

ruler_max_new.note: v1.1.2 (Dylan, 2026-10-07): RULER cells registered from 1.1.2 cap generation for the two single-answer NIAH tasks at 32 tokens; every other task keeps RULER's tokens_to_generate (niah 128, vt 30, cwe 120, fwe 50, qa 32). Raw-format Qwen runs never emit end-of-turn, so these arms generated 128 tokens to score answers of 8-9. Basis: truncating the 3,556 NIAH arm-rows of FINAL-QWEN3-8B-RULER to these budgets changed 1 row and no arm's score (checks/ruler-gen-cap.md in the paper workspace). Cells registered before 1.1.2 ran at RULER's budgets and are not re-run.
